mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in tightening periods compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of rising unemployment compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in real GDP by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and consumer demand decline.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of GDP contraction compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% month-over-month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of increased industrial production compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment, indicated by CPIAUCSL remaining below 2% for three consecutive months, suggests a stable economic environment conducive to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in low inflation periods compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and a decrease in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 5% each within the last month indicates a shift in consumer spending from goods to housing, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the housing sector strengthens.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increase > 5% and RSAFS decrease > 5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of increased housing starts and decreased retail sales compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in the last month, coupled with an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3%, signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investor sentiment turns negative.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decrease > 100k and UNRATE increase > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of declining payrolls and rising unemployment compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending supports economic growth.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increase > 1% MoM for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of sustained retail sales growth compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
